title: Corteva remains a 'buy' as innovation offsets pressure on legacy products, BofA says
detail:
Corteva remains a 'buy' as innovation offsets pressure on legacy products, BofA says
Proactive
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 10:52 AM MST
CTVA
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Corteva remains a 'buy' as innovation offsets pressure on legacy products, BofA says Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America (BofA) keeps its 'buy' rating on Corteva Inc (NYSE:CTVA) and sets an $18 price target, citing new product launches and tighter 2027 agriculture markets.

Corteva, the US crop protection company, became a focused crop protection business on October 1, after separating its seed business into Vylor.

The analyst said the price target was adjusted to reflect the separation of Vylor and values Corteva at 8.5 times estimated 2027 EBITDA.

That multiple is below the 10.5 times 2026 EBITDA previously used for Corteva in a sum-of-the-parts valuation, which values each business separately.

The analyst assumes long-term debt of $868 million and a modest net cash position, and expects the investment-grade balance sheet to support further shareholder returns.

Management targets revenue growth of 3%, EBITDA growth of 6% and an EBITDA margin of about 18% by 2029, although the analyst takes a more conservative view.

The main concern is whether new products can offset sales lost as customers switch from older Corteva products, and pressure from competitors in the existing portfolio.

The analyst views Corteva's product pipeline favorably, expecting it to broaden the portfolio and replace some legacy molecules as insect pressure and herbicide resistance increase.

Fungal diseases are also hard for seed traits to address, which leaves room for new crop protection products.

Poor farm economics and dry weather could leave inventories elevated in some markets as 2026 ends.

Tighter grain markets in 2027 could lift global volumes, and the analyst expects product launches to gain momentum into 2028.

Corteva also has significant exposure to the grain cycle, which the analyst sees as supportive as the outlook for agricultural markets in 2027 becomes more bullish.

title: DraftKings upgraded to 'Buy' by BofA on prediction market opportunity
detail:
DraftKings upgraded to 'Buy' by BofA on prediction market opportunity
Proactive
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 10:00 AM MST
DKNG
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
DraftKings upgraded to 'Buy' by BofA on prediction market opportunity Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America (BofA) has upgraded Draftkings Inc (NASDAQ:DKNG) to 'buy' from 'neutral' and kept its $27 price target, citing improving prospects for prediction markets and a more attractive risk-reward after the stock's 47% decline over the past year.

BofA said prediction markets could increasingly become a "win-win" for DraftKings, with the company now established as the third-largest player while concerns about cannibalization of its core sportsbook business have eased.

The bank estimates prediction markets could generate about $400 million in fees for DraftKings in 2027, with a further $200 million to $400 million potentially coming from market-making activities.

BofA said traditional sportsbooks have grown faster than prediction markets since the start of the football season, reducing concerns that the newer products will materially weaken DraftKings' core business.

The analyst also said DraftKings would benefit if prediction markets were ultimately restricted, because removing the regulatory uncertainty would eliminate an overhang on the company's valuation.

BofA lowered its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast to $500 million from $625 million because of higher investment in prediction markets, partly offset by stronger performance from the core business.

However, it raised its 2027 adjusted EBITDA estimate to $1.15 billion from $1.05 billion, reflecting stronger core trends and expected contributions from market-making.

The bank expects DraftKings could guide to 2027 adjusted EBITDA of $1.0 billion to $1.2 billion, leaving room for continued investment while maintaining a conservative outlook for prediction markets.

BofA's $27 price target implies 45% potential upside and is based on a 12 times multiple of 2027 enterprise value to adjusted EBITDA, a modest discount to other leading disruptors.

The analyst said the recent selloff, driven by unfavorable NFL outcomes and uncertainty over prediction market investment, appeared excessive, although stronger cost discipline will be needed to support higher margins beyond 2027.

title: If I Were Starting Over in the Stock Market in My 20s, This Is the First Investing Move I'd Make
detail:
If I Were Starting Over in the Stock Market in My 20s, This Is the First Investing Move I'd Make
David Dierking, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 8:05 AM MST
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

It's usually only with the benefit of hindsight and wisdom do we understand what we should have done and what we shouldn't. Investing is a great example. Often times, we do the best we can and hope that what we're doing will get us where we want to be down the road. Unfortunately, as the saying goes "we don't know what we don't know."

As I'm in my early 50s now, I can look back at my 30 years in the financial markets and recognize there are a few do-overs I wish I could have back. I shouldn't have gotten overzealous buying tech stocks at the end of 1999. I wish I'd bought Bank of America when it was trading for around $3 a share back in 2009.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But most of all, I wish I had automated my investing process a little better and I wish I had been more aggressive with how much I saved when I had the most time on my side.

Source: Getty Images.
Make investing automatic as early as possible

A lot of people when they get their first real job think about all the things they need or want. Maybe it's a car. Maybe it's furniture for the house. Maybe you just want to enjoy being able to order DoorDash every night.

It's easy to push investing for retirement to the back burner. If you're in your early 20s and not going to need the money for at least the next 40 years, there's always time to invest later. Right? There is. But the biggest bang for your long-term investing buck comes earliest. Starting right away gives you the most time to let long-term compounding do its thing.

Here's a good example. Imagine you invest in the Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (NYSEMKT: VTI) and are able to get a 10% annual return. If you start saving $300 a month at age 25 and continue non-stop until your age 65, you'll have accumulated around $1.9 million. But if you wait until age 35 to start saving $300 a month, at age 65 you'll only have watched your investment to grow to $678,000.

That 10-year delay cost you over $1 million.

Here's another stat. If you start at age 35 and want to still get to the $1.9 million mark by the time you get to 65, you wouldn't have to set aside just $300 a month. You'd have to invest $840. The early years in your life is where you reap the biggest rewards. The more work you do to save in your 20s means more financial flexibility in the later part of your life.

IonQ (IONQ) has moved beyond being simply a bet on whether quantum computers eventually work. The company is now expanding its business into quantum computing, networking, sensing, security, and semiconductor manufacturing.

That shift helps explain why Bank of America has put a $60 price target on IONQ and why some analysts are expecting the stock to soar even higher.

Bank of America Sees More Than Just a Quantum Computer Company

Recently, Bank of America initiated coverage of IonQ with a "Buy" rating and a target price of $60. The firm pointed to IonQ's position as the largest publicly traded pure-play quantum company by revenue, while highlighting its acquisitions and expansion into networking, security, sensing, space, and foundry services. The bank also sees IonQ's semiconductor-based strategy to increase qubit counts as an important part of its long-term opportunity.

At around $43, the $60 target implies roughly 40% upside. While that looks like meaningful upside, it isn't extreme. The mean target price for the stock sits at $67, with B. Riley Securities and Rosenblatt Securities assigning the highest price target of $100, which implies a potential upside of 133% from here.

The Opportunity Is Becoming Much Larger Than Qubits

IonQ is building computers that use quantum physics to solve certain problems much faster than today's traditional computers. It also builds the hardware, software, networking, and security systems around them. In the second quarter, IonQ generated $80.1 million in revenue, a 287% increase from the same quarter a year ago. Organic revenue growth was 132%, suggesting the business was expanding rapidly, not just through acquisitions. The company generated 60% of total revenue from commercial customers, about 50% from international business, and around 25% from customers buying multiple products. IonQ ended the quarter with $485 million of RPO, compared with $122 million a year earlier. RPO is the amount of contracted business that the company can turn into revenue over time.

Quantum computing remains highly competitive, with pure-play companies like Rigetti Computing (RGTI) and D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) also expanding rapidly. However, IonQ has multiple commercial avenues that can contribute to revenue, along with a technical edge. IonQ's ambitions now extend well beyond building quantum computers. Its portfolio now stretches across quantum networking, sensing, cybersecurity, and manufacturing. This enables IonQ to create new opportunities to monetize while the most advanced fault-tolerant quantum computers are still being developed.

title: JPMorgan Chase Earned More in 2025 Than Bank of America and Wells Fargo Combined. Can the Stock Keep Outrunning Them?
detail:
JPMorgan Chase Earned More in 2025 Than Bank of America and Wells Fargo Combined. Can the Stock Keep Outrunning Them?
James Brumley, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 5:19 AM MST
BAC
JPM
WFC
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

They may all be categorized as banking stocks. But they're certainly not all performing the same. Over the past three years, shares of JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM) have measurably outperformed those of Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) and Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC). JPM stock is up nearly 130% since early October 2023, in fact, while WFC and BAC have recently dialed back their performances for this time frame to less than 100%. By slower-moving bank stock standards, that's a significant difference.

JPM data by YCharts

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

What gives?

A deeper dive into these organizations' profit profiles explains what's at work here. Moreover, how these mixes differ sets up JPMorgan shares for continued outperformance.

One of these things is not like the other

At first blush, they're all similar enough. Digging into the details of their full-year reporting, however, reveals some stark differences between these three names. Not only is JPMorgan Chase bigger than the other two banks in terms of total revenue and net income, but it is also bigger specifically because it does so much more corporate and investment banking than BofA or Wells Fargo.

Last year, well over half of JPMorgan's bottom line came from investment banking and corporate-oriented services, topping Wells Fargo's corporate and investment banking proportion of its earnings and trouncing Bank of America's 45.1%. Conversely, JPMorgan (through Chase) does relatively less consumer banking business than BofA or Wells Fargo.

Data sources: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America 2025 investor reports. Chart by author.

And this matters now and for the foreseeable future.

Although higher interest rates are generally positive for banks' lending businesses -- since it widens the profit margins on loans -- the recent uptick in interest rates may not be the boon it typically is. The economy is sluggish due to lingering inflation, crimping demand for loans. Indeed, the Mortgage Bankers Association reports applications for mortgage loans were down roughly 24% year over year last week, extending a trend that now has the MBA's purchase applications index at a new 52-week low.

You can't make money on loans you're not even being asked to extend, posing a bigger problem for Wells Fargo and JPMorgan, and an even bigger problem for Bank of America, which does more consumer-facing business.

Investing.com -- Shares of DraftKings (DKNG) climbed 5% following an upgrade from Bank of America, which shifted its rating on the sports betting giant from Neutral to Buy. Analyst Julie Hoover maintained a $27 price objective for the stock, signaling a potential 45% upside and calling the recent 47% year-over-year pullback an attractive entry point for investors.

The upgrade marks a shift in Wall Street sentiment for DraftKings, which has faced significant pressure over the past year due to uncertain investments in prediction markets (PMs) and a string of unfavorable NFL outcomes. According to Hoover, those clouds are now lifting, presenting a highly favorable risk-reward scenario.

A central pillar of BofA's renewed optimism is DraftKings' strategic positioning in the emerging prediction market space. Hoover noted that the company has firmly established itself as the third-largest player in the sector, creating what she describes as a "win-win" scenario regardless of ongoing regulatory uncertainty.

If prediction markets receive regulatory green lights and remain viable, BofA estimates the segment could generate roughly $400 million in fees for DraftKings by 2027, supplemented by an additional $200 million to $400 million from market-making activities. Crucially, early fears that prediction markets would cannibalize traditional sports betting have not materialized; since the start of the football season, traditional sportsbooks have outpaced PM growth.

Bank of America also highlighted that Wall Street estimates for the company appear to be bottoming out. DraftKings' CEO recently confirmed at an industry conference that spending on prediction market investments could be "meaningfully" higher than initially expected.  Five Top Agent Banks Subscribe, with J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley and Bank of America Leading the Rollout

NEW YORK, Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Versana today announced the launch of Versana Loan Voting, a new digital technology solution designed to automate and streamline the amendment voting process across the broadly syndicated loan (BSL) and private credit markets. Five top agent banks have already subscribed to the platform, with J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley and Bank of America leading the rollout. Now available to all market participants, Versana Loan Voting brings self-service capabilities, transparency and scalability to one of the most time-sensitive, high-volume workflows in the $9 trillion loan asset class.

Amendments to credit agreements are a common part of the corporate loan lifecycle, largely driven by refinancings, repricings, maturity extensions or restructurings. With hundreds of amendments executed by thousands of lenders annually, demand for a modern, scalable and fully digital solution has grown rapidly across the market.

Loan voting is a time-sensitive process tied to borrower requests. The asset class has historically relied on manual workflows across spreadsheets, emails, phone calls and faxes, creating delays and limiting visibility. Versana Loan Voting transforms these disparate processes by bringing them onto a single platform using lender positions sourced from agents' systems.

"With the tremendous growth in loan issuance and the number of buy-side lenders over the years, amendment volumes have reached unprecedented levels, yet the infrastructure to scale has not kept pace," said Cynthia Sachs, Founding CEO at Versana. "We are transforming loan voting execution by enabling control, transparency and speed for agents while delivering greater position accuracy, visibility and confidence for lenders."

Versana Loan Voting expedites the amendment execution process and enables participating lenders to vote more efficiently across their fund entities. The result is a faster workflow, enabling agents to launch amendments with much greater ease, track voting results in real time and manage the loan lifecycle with more control.

Through Versana Loan Voting, lenders receive automated reminders to drive faster response times, while self-service capabilities allow asset managers to seamlessly add new funds and digitally submit votes. In addition, direct integration with agents' systems eliminates timing differences and manual reconciliation of lenders' positions to accelerate execution.
